extracted.intended_audience: Navy cost analysts, HRM program managers, graduate students and researchers conducting OMB A-76 cost comparisons
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-76 cost comparison for HRMIN
extracted.subtask_description: Perform a cost-comparison study (in-house vs contract-out) of the HRMIN system in accordance with OMB Circular No. A-76 (5 Apr 1979), documenting accumulated costs, assumptions, and conclusions about the most economical performance. The work includes building in-house cost accumulations, developing contract cost estimates, and applying present-value analysis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with OMB Circular No. A-76 (5 April 1979)
rubrics_metrics.description: The activity under review must be evaluated for compliance with the Office of Management and Budget policy (Circular No. A-76 of 5 April 1979). The policy requires review of each commercial or industrial activity costing more than $100,000 by every agency which runs one to determine if existing performance continues to be in accordance with the policy and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Circular's procedural and substantive requirements when framing the cost comparison and base conclusions on the application of these requirements to the cost comparison results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a cost-comparison framework: in-house vs contract-out
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary analytic framework is a cost comparison of in-house performance costs and the costs of contracting-out the performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accumulate all relevant in-house cost elements and develop comparable contract-out cost estimates per A-76, then compare totals (and present values where required) to support conclusions about the most economical alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 'low bid' contract price in comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular No. A-76 requires that the 'low bid' be used when conducting a cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the basic contract price exceeds total in-house costs, it can be assumed that in-house performance will be less costly and completion of remaining contract-cost portions is unnecessary (except for noted exceptions such as taxes or asset disposal). Quote from text: 'OMB Circular No. A-76 requires the "low bid" be used when conducting a cost comparison.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Accumulate full in-house cost elements
rubrics_metrics.description: In-house cost accumulation must include direct labor costs, fringe benefits on labor (annual labor costs), operation overhead expenses, one-time costs and other costs, cost of capital, and insurance where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present detailed tabulations (e.g., Direct Labor Costs; Fringe Benefits on Labor; Operation Overhead Expenses; One-Time Costs and Other Costs; Cost of Capital) and ensure consistency with accounting and cost-accounting techniques referenced (e.g., managerial/cost accounting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop contract-out cost including net additional contract costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract-out cost development must produce a basic contract price and document net additional costs that must be added to the contract price to make alternatives comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contract administration costs (the study uses a 4% contract management cost), vendor taxes where applicable, and other adjustments. If the basic contract price already exceeds in-house cost, further detailing of net additional costs may be unnecessary except for the small exceptions noted by OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider federal income taxes and asset disposal proceeds as potential offsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential federal income taxes and proceeds from disposal of assets may affect the comparison outcome and are exceptions to the low-bid shortcut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate these offsets (the study uses an IRS tax rate example of 2% and assumes assets participate in GSA sharing so are not disposed). Document whether they are material; in this study they are judged immaterial and do not alter conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Present Value / Net Present Value analysis where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Discount future cash flows to present value to compare alternatives on a common time-and-cost basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study explains present-value analysis and uses a 10% discount rate as an imputed opportunity cost for government resources. Assume comparable service lives for alternatives (the study assumes a five-year life) and state the economic assumptions and limitations of PV analysis in a government context.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and document explicit assumptions (useful life, recurring costs, immortality of service companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: All assumptions used in the analysis must be explicitly stated (e.g., no changes in variable tangible costs, equal five-year life for each alternative, recurrence of costs for each year of the five-year useful life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because assumptions materially affect results, document them clearly and recommend re-evaluation (the author recommends repeating the study after about five years when usage patterns are documented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark vendor service usage and adjust benchmarks to actual usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendor-supplied benchmark usage metrics (e.g., connect time) must be compared to actual measured usage and adjusted if benchmarking is inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the study: Tymnet's benchmark calculated connect time 2.9 times too much and was adjusted accordingly. Apply similar benchmarking/ex-post adjustments when developing contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine user profile and compute usage-based contract costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract cost development includes determining the user profile and computing usage-based charges (e.g., timesharing/connect time) for the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform computations to convert user profiles into vendor-priced units (connect hours, terminal types, RJE, storage, etc.) and summarize results for the contract-cost accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include one-time (nonrecurring) and other special costs
rubrics_metrics.description: One-time costs (e.g., initial equipment, implementation, data conversion) and other nonrecurring costs must be identified and included in the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate recurring operating costs from one-time costs in tables and include amortization or appropriate treatment when comparing alternatives across the chosen evaluation horizon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether the function is inherently governmental and the availability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the service is inherently governmental and whether satisfactory commercial sources exist to provide the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a service is not inherently governmental (commercial sources exist), economic comparisons may still favor in-house performance. The study notes HRMIN 'is not inherently governmental — satisfactory commercial sources to provide the service do exist — but the most economical performance is in-house.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus the scope of cost accumulation appropriately (host-site vs user-installation costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the scope of the analysis clearly; e.g., this study focuses on the host-site operation and excludes user-installation operational costs from the host cost analysis when not germane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include costs that are outside the analysis scope unless the Circular or comparison requirements demand them; explicitly state excluded items (the study notes user installations and their operational costs are not germane to the host-site focus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use economic judgment about immaterial intangible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Intangible costs such as small cost-of-capital values or insurance may be judged immaterial to the outcome and can be treated accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document rationale for treating intangible costs as immaterial (the author judged cost of capital and insurance 'too small to be material' for the HRMIN analysis), but include them if sensitivity or PV analysis could change conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend re-evaluation and sensitivity testing over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should be re-run periodically (e.g., after five years) or when usage/technology changes to reassess the most economical performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study recommends repeating the study when a historical usage pattern for HRMIN is documented and when system revisions and technology changes may alter comparative economics.
